WHAT THIS COURSE IS

  Trading automation course for adults and professionals: build, backtest and deploy automated
  trading systems in Python, with broker APIs, risk controls and production infrastructure,
  taught as engineering, in 10-12 months.

  In one line: The systems half of quant, done properly: build, backtest and deploy automated trading systems in Python, with broker APIs, risk controls and real production discipline.

ABOUT THE PROGRAMME

  Building a strategy is one skill; running it reliably, unattended, with real safeguards is
  another, and this course teaches the second one. It is an engineering course, not a
  money-making pitch: Python for finance, technical and fundamental analysis in code, strategy
  design and rigorous backtesting, then portfolio theory and risk-management systems, machine
  learning for trading, and the part most courses skip entirely, connecting to broker APIs,
  paper trading, and building live systems with monitoring, logging, compliance awareness and
  the safeguards that stop an automated system doing real damage. Throughout, the message is
  repeated and honest: markets carry real risk of loss, backtests do not predict the future,
  and this is education, not financial advice. A finale month builds and paper-deploys a full
  automated system and sits the final exam. The pace is honest: ten teaching months at two live
  classes a week plus four to six hours of practice, with two more in hand. Problem sets,
  monthly mixed reviews, phase exams, and a final exam that decides the certificate with a free
  retest.

WHAT MAKES THIS COURSE DIFFERENT

  - The systems half done right: from backtest to reliable, monitored, unattended execution
  - Broker APIs and paper trading taught hands-on, the step most courses skip
  - Safeguards as a core topic: the controls that stop an automated system causing harm
  - Production engineering: deployment, monitoring, logging and compliance awareness
  - Honest about risk on every page: education, not financial advice, no profit claims
  - Real assessment: weekly problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams and a final exam
    with a free retest

COMMON QUESTIONS ABOUT THIS COURSE

  For anything about cost, use PART 4 and RULE 1. Do not quote two regions.

  Q: What does this trading automation course cover?
  A: The systems half of quant trading, taught as engineering: Python for finance, technical
  and fundamental analysis in code, strategy design and rigorous backtesting, portfolio theory
  and risk-management systems, machine learning for trading, then connecting to broker APIs,
  paper trading, and building live systems with monitoring, logging, compliance awareness and
  safeguards. A finale month builds and paper-deploys a full automated system and sits the
  final exam. It is education, not financial advice.

  Q: How long does it take to learn trading automation properly?
  A: Ten months of teaching at 2 live classes a week plus 4 to 6 hours of practice, with two
  more months in hand for learners who need them. The three teaching phases build the skill and
  its real-world application; the finale month ships a capstone and sits the final exam.

  Q: How am I assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
  A: No. Problem sets follow every class with written feedback, monthly reviews deliberately
  mix new material with earlier topics, each phase ends with a cumulative exam, and the course
  ends with a final exam: a practical build plus written questions from the whole syllabus.
  Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused revision and a free retest.

  Q: Is this financial advice? Will I make guaranteed profits?
  A: No, and be wary of anyone who says otherwise. This is an engineering and quantitative
  course: it teaches you to research, build, backtest and automate trading systems, not what to
  buy or a way to get rich. Markets carry real risk of loss, backtest results do not guarantee
  future returns, and we make no profit claims of any kind. What you gain is genuine, in-demand
  skill; what you do with real money afterwards is your own decision and your own risk.

  Q: How is this different from your algorithmic trading course?
  A: This course is the systems-and-execution half: how to take a strategy and run it reliably
  and safely through broker APIs, with monitoring, safeguards and production discipline. The
  algorithmic trading course is the research half: what to trade, why, and how to backtest it
  honestly. Many serious learners take both; that one makes you the researcher, this one makes
  you the systems engineer.

  Q: Do I need finance or trading experience to start?
  A: No. The markets knowledge and the maths you need are taught from the ground up. This
  course leans slightly more toward software engineering, so comfort with programming logic
  helps, but everything is taught step by step from the first class.

WHAT THIS COURSE IS

  TypeScript course for college students and professionals: JavaScript foundations, the type
  system to depth, then typed React and Node in 10-12 months.

  In one line: The language modern teams actually write: JavaScript foundations, the type system as a superpower, then typed React and Node end to end.

ABOUT THE PROGRAMME

  TypeScript won: new frontend and most serious Node work is written in it, and the type
  system, learned properly, is not bureaucracy but a superpower: bugs caught at compile time,
  refactors that stop being scary, editors that finish your thoughts. This live online
  masterclass builds it honestly: JavaScript foundations first (TypeScript is JavaScript
  underneath), then the type system to real depth, generics, narrowing, utility types, the
  honest limits, then typed application development: React with TypeScript the way product
  teams write it, and Node backends with types end to end. A finale month ships a full-stack
  typed capstone and sits the final exam. The pace is honest: ten teaching months at two live
  classes a week plus four to six hours of practice, with two more in hand. Problem sets,
  monthly mixed reviews, phase exams, and a final exam that decides the certificate with a free
  retest.

WHAT MAKES THIS COURSE DIFFERENT

  - JavaScript first, honestly: TypeScript without JS depth is decoration
  - The type system as a skill: generics and narrowing understood, not copy-pasted
  - Typed both ends: React and Node with types flowing end to end
  - Real-team habits: strictness levels, migration judgment, when any is a lie
  - An honest 10-month arc with 2 months in hand
  - Real assessment: weekly problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams and a final exam
    with a free retest

THE LEARNING PATH, STEP BY STEP

  Phase 1: Foundations (Months 1-3): JavaScript properly, then TypeScript fundamentals
  Phase 2: Typed frontend (Months 4-6): React with TypeScript as product teams write it
  Phase 3: Typed backend (Months 7-9): Node and Express with types end to end
  Phase 4: The finale (Month 10): a full-stack typed capstone and the final exam

WHAT A STUDENT NEEDS BEFORE STARTING

  Coding experience: None. Everything is taught from the first line
  Equipment: Any computer with a stable internet connection; every tool used is free
  Age: 18+; college students, graduates and working professionals
  Time commitment: 2 live classes plus 4-6 hours of practice a week

WHO THIS COURSE IS FOR

  Js developers: JavaScript developers making the move every team already made
  College students: Students who want the hiring default, not the legacy path
  Self taught: Tutorial-experienced learners ready for the discipline layer
  Backend bound: Developers who want typed Node without the framework fog
  Career switchers: Professionals entering web development at the modern baseline

  A: Ten months of teaching at 2 live classes a week plus 4 to 6 hours of practice, with two
  more months in hand for learners who need them. The three teaching phases build the skill and
  its real-world application; the finale month ships a capstone and sits the final exam.

  Q: Should I learn JavaScript first, or start directly with TypeScript?
  A: This course settles it: you learn JavaScript properly inside it, then add types. Starting
  with TypeScript syntax over weak JavaScript produces developers who fight the compiler;
  learning JS first then typing it produces developers the compiler helps. That order is the
  course.

WHAT THIS COURSE IS

  Vedic maths course online with live classes: all 16 sutras for fast multiplication, squares,
  division and mental calculation. Ages 8 to adult, free demo class.

  In one line: The same sums, done in a third of the time, with a method you can check.

ABOUT THE PROGRAMME

  Vedic maths is a system of calculation shortcuts organised around 16 sutras, short working
  rules like Nikhilam (all from 9 and the last from 10) and Urdhva-Tiryagbhyam (vertically and
  crosswise). Used well, they turn sums like 97 x 96 or 998 squared into a few seconds of
  mental work. This 6-month live course teaches the system the way a maths teacher would: every
  shortcut is shown, practised against the clock, and then explained, because a student who
  knows why a trick works can trust it in an exam and adapt it when the numbers change. The
  course runs in one straight line: multiplication shortcuts first, because they pay off
  fastest, then squares and cubes, then division including the flag method, then fractions,
  decimals and percentages at speed, and finally the algebra applications of the same sutras.
  Week 1 starts with a timed diagnostic; week 24 ends with the same style of paper, so every
  student can see exactly how much faster and more accurate they have become. We are honest
  about what this course is: it makes arithmetic faster and frees up exam time. It does not
  replace school maths, and it will not turn anyone into a prodigy. It rewards steady drill,
  and we structure that drill for you.

WHAT MAKES THIS COURSE DIFFERENT

  - Every shortcut comes with its reason: students see the algebra behind Nikhilam and the duplex
    method, so the rules stick instead of jumbling together
  - Timed drills from week 1, with a personal speed log so progress is measured against your own
    diagnostic, not against a claim
  - We teach judgement, not just tricks: which sutra fits which sum, and when the ordinary school
    method is actually the better choice
  - Digit-sum checking is built in from the start, so speed never comes at the cost of accuracy
  - Mixed-age friendly: the same system is drilled at school-exam pace for children and at
    competitive-exam pace for older students
  - Live small-group classes where the teacher watches you calculate, catches bad habits early,
    and adjusts the drill sheets to your errors

THE LEARNING PATH, STEP BY STEP

  Phase 1: The multiplication engine: complements, Nikhilam base multiplication, special
  patterns, then Urdhva-Tiryagbhyam for any numbers, all against the clock
  Phase 2: Squares, cubes and roots with Yavadunam and the duplex method, then division three
  ways: Nikhilam, Paravartya and the flag method
  Phase 3: Fractions, decimals and percentages at speed, the algebra applications of the
  sutras, and a timed capstone measured against the week 1 diagnostic

WHAT A STUDENT NEEDS BEFORE STARTING

  Maths level: Comfortable addition and subtraction, and multiplication tables up to 10. That
    is genuinely all
  Age: 8 to adult. Batches are grouped by age so drills run at the right pace
  Equipment: A notebook, a pen, and a device with a camera and stable internet for live classes
  Prior vedic maths: None expected. The course starts from the first sutra

WHO THIS COURSE IS FOR

  School students: Students in classes 3 to 10 who lose exam time to slow arithmetic and want
    it back
  Competitive exam aspirants: Older students preparing for arithmetic-heavy MCQ exams where a
    saved minute per section matters
  Parents learning alongside: Adults who want to sharpen mental arithmetic, sometimes in the
    same batch as their child
  Students who fear calculation: Children who understand concepts but freeze on big
    multiplications; the drills rebuild confidence with evidence
  Maths enjoyers: Students who simply like numbers and want to know why the shortcuts work, not
    just that they do

COMMON QUESTIONS ABOUT THIS COURSE

  For anything about cost, use PART 4 and RULE 1. Do not quote two regions.

  Q: What is Vedic maths, honestly?
  A: It is a system of 16 sutras, short calculation rules, compiled by Bharati Krishna Tirthaji
  and published in 1965. Historians debate how ancient the system really is, and we say so in
  class, because the techniques stand on their own: they are fast, they are checkable, and
  every one of them has ordinary algebra underneath. We teach the methods and the algebra, not
  the mythology.

  Q: Will this replace my child's school maths?
  A: No, and it should not. School maths teaches concepts and requires standard working in
  answers; this course makes the arithmetic inside those answers faster and more accurate. We
  explicitly teach when to use a shortcut, when to show the standard method, and how to use
  digit-sum checks on both. Think of it as removing the calculation bottleneck from maths a
  student is already learning.

  Q: Does Vedic maths actually help in competitive exams?
  A: It helps with one specific thing: calculation speed in arithmetic-heavy sections, which
  frees minutes for the questions that need real thought. It does not teach exam concepts,
  shortcuts for reasoning, or anything a syllabus tests directly. Students preparing for MCQ
  exams tend to feel the benefit most in percentages, fractions and multiplication-heavy
  questions, which is exactly where phase 3 of this course spends its time.

  Q: Will this course make my child a genius or a human calculator?
  A: No, and we would rather tell you that upfront. What steady practice on this course
  produces is documented in each student's speed log: the same kinds of sums done faster and
  with fewer errors than in week 1. That is a real, useful, measurable gain. Claims beyond
  that, about IQ or brain development, are not ones we make.

  Q: What age is right for this course?
  A: We take students from age 8, once multiplication tables are reasonably solid, and there is
  no upper limit; adults join to sharpen mental arithmetic, sometimes in the same house as an
  enrolled child. Batches are grouped by age so an 8-year-old drills at a different pace from a
  16-year-old preparing for entrance exams.

  Q: How is Vedic maths different from abacus classes?
  A: Abacus training builds mental arithmetic through a physical tool and bead visualisation,
  and it works best when started young, roughly ages 5 to 10. Vedic maths is paper-and-head
  arithmetic built on algebraic patterns, so it suits any age that knows its tables and extends
  naturally into algebra. Younger children often do abacus first and Vedic maths later; we run
  both and will honestly tell you which fits your child.

  Q: My child already struggles with maths. Is a speed course a bad idea?
  A: Often it is the opposite, with one condition: the struggles must be with calculation, not
  with concepts. A child who understands what multiplication means but dreads big numbers
  usually gains confidence quickly here, because the methods are short and the progress is
  visible in their own log. If the gaps are conceptual, we will say so after the demo class and
  point you to our school maths courses instead.

  Q: How am I assessed, and is the certificate just for showing up?
  A: No. A task follows every class with feedback, monthly reviews deliberately mix new
  material with earlier topics so nothing is forgotten, and the course ends with a final exam
  covering the whole course. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused
  revision and a free retest. We measure real learning, not attendance.

  Q: Can we try a class before enrolling?
  A: Yes, the first demo class is free and carries no obligation. Book it at
  learn.modernagecoders.com/contact or message us on WhatsApp at +91 91233 66161. Parents are
  welcome to sit in, and the teacher will give you a straight opinion on whether this course or
  a school maths course is the better fit.

  To enrol, message Shivam Sir on +91 9123366161 or send the parent this link: https://learn.modernagecoders.com/courses/vedic-maths-course-speed-calculation-mastery
  For a demo: the Priority Live Demo (guaranteed, today or tomorrow) is booked at
  https://learn.modernagecoders.com/priority-demo . The free demo is a waiting list with no fixed date.

  Vibe Coding for College is the most comprehensive 3-month software engineering program for
  college students and fresh graduates aged 18+. 'Vibe Coding', coined by AI pioneer Andrej
  Karpathy in 2025, means building software by describing what you want in natural language and
  letting AI generate the code. In 2026, this has evolved into 'agentic engineering',
  orchestrating multiple AI agents to build production-grade software at startup speed. This
  course teaches you both: deep engineering fundamentals AND professional-grade AI development
  tools. You will master the MERN stack using Cursor IDE (the #1 AI code editor), accelerate
  development with Claude Code (Anthropic's terminal-based AI engineer), prototype at speed

  Q: What is Vibe Coding for College?
  A: Vibe Coding for College is a 3-month, intensive software engineering program for college
  students and fresh graduates (18+). It uniquely combines deep engineering fundamentals with
  professional AI development tools: you master MERN stack using Cursor IDE and Claude Code,
  build rapid prototypes with Lovable and Bolt.new, learn DSA for placements, Machine Learning
  with Python, System Design, and security for AI-generated code, all taught live by
  industry-experienced mentors at Modern Age Coders.

  Q: Who is this course for?
  A: This course is for college students (any year) and recent graduates who know at least
  basic programming and want to break into software engineering. It's ideal for CS/IT/MCA
  students, but engineering students from any branch who are serious about tech can join. You
  should have basic knowledge of at least one programming language (Python, Java, C++, or
  JavaScript).

  Q: What is the MERN stack and why learn it?
  A: MERN stands for MongoDB (database), Express.js (backend framework), React.js (frontend
  library), and Node.js (JavaScript runtime). It is the most popular and in-demand full-stack
  technology combination for 2026, used by top startups and tech companies worldwide. MERN
  skills are specifically sought in Indian product companies, MNCs, and international remote
  roles.

  Q: How does DSA preparation fit into this course?
  A: DSA is integrated throughout all 12 weeks rather than crammed at the end. Weeks 5-6 are
  dedicated DSA weeks, but we recommend 10 problems per week from Week 1 onwards through our
  parallel preparation track. By Week 12, students have typically solved 100-150 problems
  across LeetCode, GeeksforGeeks, and Codeforces.

  Q: Will studying 3 months really prepare me for placements?
  A: Three months of focused, structured preparation, building real projects, solving 100+ DSA
  problems, and doing mock interviews, is absolutely transformative. Join as early in your
  college career as possible: students who take this course in their 2nd or 3rd year have
  maximally more time to practice and build. Our alumni have been placed at companies including
  Infosys, TCS, Wipro, Freshworks, Juspay, and international remote companies.

  Q: What does 'Vibe Coding' mean at the college level?
  A: Vibe Coding, coined by Andrej Karpathy in 2025, means building software by describing what
  you want and letting AI generate the code. At the college level, this evolves into 'agentic
  engineering': using professional AI tools (Cursor IDE, Claude Code, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot)
  alongside AI app builders (Lovable, Bolt.new, v0.dev) to build production-grade software at
  startup speed. But the key differentiator is that you also learn to REVIEW, SECURE, and SCALE
  what AI generates, because 45% of AI-generated code contains security vulnerabilities. You
  graduate as a developer who can build with AI AND without it.

  Q: Do you help with interview and career preparation?
  A: Week 11 is dedicated to career preparation: resume reviews, LinkedIn optimization, mock
  technical interviews, system design practice, and DSA rapid revision. You also get access to
  our alumni network and mentor panels. We prepare you thoroughly for interviews and
  applications, but we do not guarantee placement.

  Q: What is the time commitment?
  A: We recommend 10-15 hours per week: 2 live sessions (2 hours each), weekly DSA practice
  (3-4 hours), and project work (4-6 hours). This is an intensive program. The more you invest,
  the stronger your portfolio and placement readiness will be.

  Q: Is Machine Learning part of this course?
  A: Yes. Weeks 7 and 8 cover applied Machine Learning with Python, scikit-learn, regression,
  classification, clustering, neural networks with TensorFlow/Keras, and deploying ML models as
  APIs and web apps. This is applied/practical ML, not theory-heavy research ML.

  Q: What certification will I receive?
  A: This is a credential recognized by our industry partners and verifiable online.

ABOUT THE PROGRAMME

  Vibe Coding for Kids is the ultimate 3-month beginner coding journey designed specifically
  for children aged 8 to 12. 'Vibe Coding', a term coined by AI pioneer Andrej Karpathy in
  2025, means telling a computer what you want to build in plain English and letting AI create
  the code for you. It's the future of how software gets made, and your child can start
  learning it now. Through playful, visual, and project-driven learning, kids discover the
  magic of creating their own games, animated stories, music with code, and real AI-powered
  apps, no complex typing required to get started! Kids begin with visual block coding
  (Scratch) to learn how computers think, then graduate to actual vibe coding using tools like
  Replit, Bolt.new, and Google Gemini, the same AI tools professionals use today. At Modern Age
  Coders, we believe every child is a natural creator. Our expert instructors blend visual
  block programming, creative exploration, and real AI app-building tools to make coding feel
  like play. By the end of 12 weeks, your child will have built 15+ original projects,
  including apps they built by talking to AI, and gained real digital superpowers.

WHAT MAKES THIS COURSE DIFFERENT

  - 100% project-based, kids build something real every single week
  - Age-appropriate content designed for 8-12 year olds
  - No prior experience or technical knowledge needed
  - Visual block coding (Scratch, Code.org), no complex syntax to start
  - Real vibe coding: kids build apps by talking to AI (Replit, Bolt.new)
  - Includes AI tools, music coding, and creative art projects
  - Live classes with expert instructors, never pre-recorded videos
  - Weekly written progress notes to parents
  - Portfolio of 15+ completed projects at course end
  - Fun, encouraging, and bully-free classroom environment

  Bolt.new), AI tools, music coding, capstone project showcase

FULL CURRICULUM, WEEK BY WEEK

  This is the complete teaching plan. Parents can ask about any week.

  ---------------------------------------------------------------
  PHASE 1: FOUNDATION VIBES, SCRATCH & CREATIVE CODING (WEEKS 1-4)
  ---------------------------------------------------------------
  Kids dive into the colourful world of Scratch and block-based programming. They create their
  first animations, interactive stories, and simple games while learning the core ideas of
  coding, loops, events, and conditionals, through hands-on fun.

    Week 1: Welcome to Vibe Coding!, Your First Animations
      Topics:
        - What is Vibe Coding?, Telling computers what to build using your words (coined by AI
          scientist Andrej Karpathy in 2025)
        - The two ways to code: Block Coding (Scratch) and Vibe Coding (talking to AI), we'll learn
          both!
        - How computers think, understanding instructions step by step
        - Introduction to Scratch 3.0, navigating the interface
        - Sprites, stages, and backdrops, building your digital world
        - Basic motion blocks: move, turn, glide
        - Looks blocks: say, think, costumes, effects
        - Sound blocks: play music, record your voice
        - Your first animation: Make a character walk and talk
        - Saving and sharing your Scratch project
        - Online safety and being a kind digital citizen
        - Setting up your Vibe Coder profile
      Projects built:
        - Animated Greeting Card, make a character say hello to the world
        - Dancing Pet, a sprite that moves to your favourite music
        - About Me Story, an interactive presentation about yourself
      Practice: Build a mini dance party in Scratch where your sprite changes costume and moves
      each time you press an arrow key, then show someone at home.

    Week 2: Storytelling with Code, Scenes, Dialogues & Adventures
      Topics:
        - Creating multi-scene stories with backdrop changes
        - Broadcasting messages between sprites, making characters talk to each other
        - Using the 'ask and answer' block for interactive dialogue
        - Timing animations, wait blocks and synchronized stories
        - Creating sprite costumes for character emotions
        - Adding background music and sound effects
        - Text-to-speech: making your characters speak in different voices
        - Importing your own images and drawings as sprites
        - Drawing custom sprites with the Scratch paint editor
        - Story planning: beginning, middle, and end
        - Sharing your story with family and friends
      Projects built:
        - A 3-Scene Adventure Story, hero, challenge, and victory
        - Interactive Storybook, click to turn pages
        - Talking Animal Show, two animals have a funny conversation
      Practice: Create a two scene story where characters talk to each other using broadcast
      messages and ask the viewer one question with the ask block.

    Week 3: Events & Interactivity, Making Things Happen!
      Topics:
        - Event blocks: when green flag clicked, when key pressed, when sprite clicked
        - Keyboard controls, making characters move with arrow keys
        - Mouse events, click-to-activate actions
        - Creating clickable buttons and navigation menus
        - Introduction to conditionals: If-Then logic blocks
        - Touching and color detection, collision basics
        - Creating interactive art, drawing with mouse movements
        - Building a virtual musical keyboard
        - Combining multiple events for complex interactions
        - User input with 'ask' and storing answers
        - Debugging basics: What to do when something goes wrong
      Projects built:
        - Virtual Piano, play notes by pressing keyboard keys
        - Click-and-Colour Art Canvas, draw with code
        - Interactive Quiz, 5 questions with right/wrong feedback
      Practice: Make a clickable pet that reacts differently to a click, a key press and the
      green flag, using at least one if then block.

    Week 4: Loops & Patterns, The Magic of Repetition
      Topics:
        - Forever loops, making things go on and on
        - Repeat loops with a specific number of times
        - Nested loops, loops inside loops for complex patterns
        - Drawing geometric shapes with pen blocks
        - Creating spirals, stars, and kaleidoscopes with loops
        - The Stamp tool, making repeating patterns
        - Color effects and graphic transformations
        - Thinking like a computer: breaking big tasks into small loops
        - Efficiency, doing more with less code
        - Creating a looping background animation
        - Phase 1 Review & Project Planning
      Projects built:
        - Geometric Art Machine, generates beautiful patterns automatically
        - Spinning Galaxy, looping space animation
        - Pattern Puzzle, create a design and challenge friends to recreate it
      Practice: Draw a star, a spiral and one invented pattern with pen blocks inside repeat
      loops, and name your favorite creation.

  ---------------------------------------------------------------
  PHASE 2: GAME DEV VIBES, BUILD YOUR OWN GAMES! (WEEKS 5-8)
  ---------------------------------------------------------------
  Now the real fun begins! Kids learn the building blocks of game development: scoring, lives,
  enemies, levels, and game loops. By the end of Phase 2, every child will have built a
  complete, playable video game from scratch.

    Week 5: Variables & Score Systems, 'You Win!' Moments
      Topics:
        - What are variables? Understanding data storage in simple terms
        - Creating score, lives, and timer variables
        - Changing variable values, adding points, losing lives
        - Using random numbers, the element of surprise in games
        - Countdown timers and time-based challenges
        - Displaying variables on screen as a score HUD
        - Win conditions: What happens when you reach a goal?
        - Game Over conditions: Lives system and health bars
        - High score saving basics
        - Creating power-ups that boost your score
        - Playtesting your games, the 'fun factor' check
      Projects built:
        - Catch the Falling Stars, catch sprites to earn points
        - Number Guessing Game, with hints and score tracking
        - Speed Challenge, collect 10 items before the timer runs out
      Practice: Add a score, lives and a countdown timer to a simple catch the apple game and
      play test it three times.

    Week 6: Collision Detection & Game Mechanics, Real Game Feels
      Topics:
        - Touching detection, sprites interacting with each other
        - Color collision, detecting when you touch a wall or obstacle
        - Gravity simulation using loops and variables
        - Jumping mechanics, platformer physics basics
        - Enemy movement, creating obstacles that move and follow
        - Projectile mechanics, shooting and throwing
        - Boundary detection, keeping sprites inside the screen
        - Creating a scrolling background effect
        - Power-up pickups and damage effects
        - Sound effects for collisions, wins, and game over
        - Making your game feel satisfying, game juice basics
      Projects built:
        - The Endless Runner, dodge obstacles as you run
        - Space Invaders Jr., shoot incoming aliens
        - Trampoline Jump, bounce as high as you can game
      Practice: Give your game character a gravity powered jump and one moving enemy that ends
      the game on touch.

    Week 7: Level Design & Multi-Screen Games, The Full Experience
      Topics:
        - What makes a great game level? Flow, challenge, and reward
        - Designing level 1, level 2, and level 3 with increasing difficulty
        - Using backdrops as levels, switching on game events
        - Creating boss levels and final challenges
        - Save and load game states using cloud variables
        - Cutscenes and story sequences between levels
        - Sound design, choosing music for different game moods
        - UI design: Start screen, game over screen, victory screen
        - Multiple character selection screens
        - Accessibility in games, making your game easy to understand
        - Beta testing with classmates and collecting feedback
      Projects built:
        - 3-Level Maze Adventure, escape each dungeon to advance
        - Fruit Ninja Clone, 3 difficulty levels with progressive speed
        - Boss Battle Game, survive the final boss to win
      Practice: Design level 1 and a harder level 2 for your game using two backdrops that
      switch when the player wins.

    Week 8: Complete Game Jam, Build Your Dream Game!
      Topics:
        - Game design document, planning your game on paper first
        - Asset creation, custom sprites, backgrounds, and sounds
        - Implementing full game loop: start, play, lose, win
        - Bug hunting and debugging strategies
        - Game polishing, making it look professional
        - Writing game instructions for players
        - Creating a game thumbnail and cover art
        - Publishing your game to the Scratch community
        - Presenting your game to classmates
        - Getting featured on the Modern Age Coders showcase
        - Reflecting on your journey from Week 1 to Week 8
      Projects built:

ABOUT THE PROGRAMME

  There is a special kind of pride in a child saying "I made this website", and meaning typed,
  real, published code. This live online course gives that to children aged 9 to 12: HTML
  learned as the structure of every page, CSS as the art layer, layouts with flexbox and grid,
  responsive design tested on the family phone, and first JavaScript, the sparks that make
  pages respond. Every project is hand-typed by the child; this course builds real skill, not
  copy-paste. Publishing is the heartbeat: pages go live to real web addresses the family can
  visit, and the course ends with a capstone site, planned, built, polished and presented at
  demo day. Near the end, one honest week looks ahead at how professional developers use AI
  assistants, including why those tools have age rules (most are 13+, some 18+) and why the
  skills built in this course are exactly what will make such tools useful later. Nothing in
  the course requires any AI account, because nine-year-olds should be building their own
  skill, and the tools' own rules agree. The pace is honest and kid-sized: eight months at two
  live classes a week plus two to three hours of playful practice, with two more months in hand
  when needed. Homework after every class, a mixed challenge at the end of each month, and a
  final exam, a capstone demo plus a friendly viva, that decides the certificate, with a free
  retest after revision. Real code, real websites, real pride.

WHAT MAKES THIS COURSE DIFFERENT

  - Real typed code from day one: no drag-and-drop site builders, no copy-paste dependence
  - Publishing as a habit: children's pages go live at real web addresses their family can visit
  - Kid-sized honest pace: 8 months at 2 classes a week, with 2 more in hand when needed
  - Age-honest about AI: one look-ahead week explains how developers use AI assistants and why
    those tools are 13+ and 18+, no child accounts required or used
  - Design taste built alongside code: spacing, color and layout judged out loud, kindly
  - Real assessment, gently done: monthly mixed challenges and a final capstone exam with a free
    retest

THE LEARNING PATH, STEP BY STEP

  Phase 1: HTML world (Months 1-2): structure, text, images, links, forms and multimedia,
  hand-typed from the first day
  Phase 2: CSS magic (Months 3-4): color, typography, the box model, flexbox and grid
  Phase 3: JavaScript sparks (Months 5-6): responsive design, then first real programming:
  logic, loops and little games
  Phase 4: Real sites (Months 7-8): functions and DOM magic, publishing properly, the AI
  look-ahead, and the capstone exam

WHAT A STUDENT NEEDS BEFORE STARTING

  Coding experience: None. The course starts at the very first tag
  Reading typing: Comfortable reading; typing improves fast within the course
  Equipment: A computer or laptop with a stable internet connection; every tool used is free
  Age: 9 to 12. Younger children start better in our Kids Coding (Scratch-first) course
  Time commitment: 2 live classes plus 2-3 hours of playful practice a week

WHO THIS COURSE IS FOR

  Young builders: Children who want to make real things the whole family can visit online
  Scratch graduates: Kids who finished block coding and are hungry for real typed code
  Creative kids: Children who love drawing and design, CSS is where art meets code
  Future teens: Kids who will roll naturally into our teen web and full-stack courses
  Proud families: Parents who want screen time producing published, showable work

FULL CURRICULUM, WEEK BY WEEK

  This is the complete teaching plan. Parents can ask about any week.

  ---------------------------------------------------------------
  PHASE 1: HTML WORLD (MONTHS 1-2, WEEKS 1-8)
  ---------------------------------------------------------------
  The structure of every website, hand-typed: text, images, links, forms, tables and
  multimedia, each week ending with a page to show the family.

    Month 1: First Pages (Weeks 1-4)
      Welcome to Web Development
        Topics:
          - What is a website? How does the internet work (kid-friendly explanation)
          - Setting up your coding playground: VS Code with fun themes
          - Installing colorful extensions and emoji support
          - Your first HTML file: Hello World with emojis!
          - Understanding tags: like LEGO blocks for websites
          - Creating a personal 'About Me' page
          - HTML structure: <html>, <head>, <body> explained with stories
          - Saving and viewing your first webpage
          - Celebrating your first website with screenshots!
          - Typing practice for young coders: a little every day
        Projects built:
          - Build a digital pet profile page
          - Make a birthday invitation webpage
      HTML Elements Zoo - Text, Images & Links
        Topics:
          - Heading tags (h1-h6): Creating titles like newspaper headlines
          - Paragraph tag: Writing stories on your webpage
          - Making lists: Favorite games, friends, hobbies (ul, ol, li)
          - Bold and italic: Making text stand out (strong, em)
          - Adding images: Your photos, drawings, and GIFs
          - Image attributes: alt text for accessibility
          - Creating links: Connect your pages like a treasure map
          - Link to other websites: YouTube, games, educational sites
          - Making a photo album webpage
          - Building a collection of favorite things
        Projects built:
          - Digital photo album with captions
          - My favorite YouTube videos collection
          - Interactive storybook with multiple pages
          - School project presentation website
        Practice: Build 5 themed pages (animals, sports, hobbies, etc.)
        Assessment: Month 1 check: build a small page live from a sketch, plus a fun take-home
        challenge

    Month 2: HTML Powers (Weeks 5-8)
      Fun with Forms & Tables
        Topics:
          - Creating forms: Like making a quiz for friends
          - Input types: text, email, password, number
          - Fun input types: color picker, date picker, range slider
          - Checkboxes for multiple choices: Pizza toppings selector
          - Radio buttons for single choice: Favorite superhero poll
          - Dropdown menus: Choose your adventure options
          - Textarea: Writing stories and comments
          - Tables for organizing information: Sports scores, schedules
          - Making tables pretty with borders and colors
          - Building interactive surveys
        Projects built:
          - Friend information collector form
          - Class schedule table
          - Restaurant menu with order form
        Practice: Create 5 different interactive forms
      Multimedia Magic - Audio, Video & Canvas
        Topics:
          - Adding videos to your webpage: YouTube embeds
          - HTML5 video tag: Playing your own videos
          - Audio elements: Adding music and sound effects
          - Creating playlists on your webpage
          - Canvas basics: Drawing on webpages
          - Embedding games and interactive content
          - iframe: Windows to other websites
          - Making a multimedia gallery
          - Creating a personal YouTube-style page
          - Building an online portfolio of creations
        Projects built:
          - Personal video channel page
          - Music playlist website
          - Digital art gallery with canvas
          - Multimedia learning resource page
        Practice: Add multimedia to all previous projects
        Assessment: Month 2 check: a multimedia page built live, with quiz questions reaching
        back to month 1

  ---------------------------------------------------------------
  PHASE 2: CSS MAGIC (MONTHS 3-4, WEEKS 9-16)
  ---------------------------------------------------------------
  The art layer: colors, fonts, the box model, then the two great layout tools, flexbox and
  grid, used to make pages genuinely beautiful.

    Month 3: Style Arrives (Weeks 9-12)
      CSS Basics - Making Websites Beautiful
        Topics:
          - What is CSS? The fashion designer for HTML
          - Three ways to add CSS: inline, internal, external stylesheets
          - CSS syntax: selector { property: value; }
          - Selecting elements: tags, classes, and IDs
          - Colors everywhere: background-color, color
          - Color codes: named colors, hex codes, RGB
          - Font families: Changing how text looks
          - Google Fonts: Adding fun fonts to websites
          - Text size, weight, and style
          - Text alignment and decoration
        Projects built:
          - Rainbow text website
          - Colorful mood board page
          - Typography playground
        Practice: Style 10 HTML pages with different themes
      CSS Box Model & Spacing Magic
        Topics:
          - The Box Model: Every element is a box!
          - Padding: Space inside the box
          - Margin: Space outside the box
          - Border: The box's frame (styles, colors, radius)
          - Width and height: Sizing your boxes
          - Making round corners with border-radius
          - Creating shapes with CSS: circles, triangles
          - Box shadows for 3D effects
          - Background images and patterns
          - Building card-based layouts
        Projects built:
          - Trading card collection webpage
          - Social media profile page clone
          - Product showcase with cards
          - CSS art project with shapes
        Practice: Create 10 different card designs
        Assessment: Month 3 check: style a plain page live to match a design, plus mixed review

    Month 4: Layout Superpowers (Weeks 13-16)
      Flexbox - The Flexible Layout System
        Topics:
          - Introduction to Flexbox: Making layouts flexible
          - Flex container and flex items
          - Flex-direction: row, column, reverse
          - Justify-content: Spacing items horizontally
          - Align-items: Spacing items vertically
          - Creating navigation bars with Flexbox
          - Building photo galleries
          - Flexbox games: Flexbox Froggy, Flexbox Defense
          - Making responsive card layouts
          - Creating hero sections
        Projects built:
          - Responsive navigation menu
          - Pinterest-style photo gallery
          - Flexible dashboard layout
          - Game character selection screen
        Practice: Complete all Flexbox Froggy levels
      CSS Grid - The Ultimate Layout Tool
        Topics:
          - CSS Grid basics: Rows and columns
          - Grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows
          - Grid gaps: Adding space between items
          - Placing items in specific grid cells
          - Grid areas: Naming your layout sections
          - Creating magazine-style layouts
          - Building game boards with Grid
          - Grid Garden game for practice
          - Combining Flexbox and Grid
          - Responsive grids with auto-fit
          - Creating complex layouts easily
        Projects built:
          - Magazine homepage layout
          - Tic-tac-toe game board
          - Calendar layout with Grid
          - Minecraft-style inventory grid
        Practice: Build 10 different grid layouts
        Assessment: Month 4 check: build a card layout live with flexbox or grid, plus mixed
        review

  ---------------------------------------------------------------
  PHASE 3: JAVASCRIPT SPARKS (MONTHS 5-6, WEEKS 17-24)
  ---------------------------------------------------------------
  Pages that fit every screen, then the big step: first real programming, decisions, loops and
  little games, in the language of the web.

    Month 5: Every Screen, First Code (Weeks 17-20)
      Responsive Design - Mobile First!
        Topics:
          - What is responsive design? One site for all devices
          - Mobile-first approach: Start small, go big
          - Media queries: Different styles for different screens
          - Breakpoints: Phone, tablet, desktop
          - Responsive units: %, vw, vh, rem, em
          - Responsive images: srcset and picture element
          - Responsive typography: Scaling text
          - Testing on different devices
          - Chrome DevTools device simulator
          - Mobile-friendly navigation patterns
          - Touch-friendly button sizes
        Projects built:
          - Responsive portfolio website
          - Mobile-first blog layout
          - Adaptive gaming website
          - Responsive school project site
        Practice: Make all previous projects responsive
      JavaScript Basics - Making Websites Interactive
        Topics:
          - What is JavaScript? The brain of websites
          - Adding JavaScript to HTML pages
          - Console.log: Talking to the computer
          - Variables: Storing information (let, const)
          - Data types: Numbers, strings, booleans
          - Basic math operations
          - String concatenation: Joining words
          - Template literals: Easy text formatting
          - Comments in JavaScript
        Projects built:
          - Interactive calculator
          - Mad libs story generator
          - Age calculator with messages
          - Simple greeting program
        Practice: Write 20 simple JavaScript programs
        Assessment: Month 5 check: make a page respond to a click live, plus mixed review of
        earlier months

    Month 6: Logic, Loops and Little Games (Weeks 21-24)
      JavaScript Logic & Decisions
        Topics:
          - If statements: Making decisions
          - Else and else if: Multiple choices
          - Comparison operators: >, <, ==, ===
          - Logical operators: AND (&&), OR (||), NOT (!)
          - Switch statements for multiple cases
          - Ternary operator: Quick decisions
          - Random numbers with Math.random()
          - Building simple games with logic
          - Creating quiz logic
          - Score keeping systems
        Projects built:
          - Rock, Paper, Scissors game
          - Number guessing game
          - Quiz with scoring
          - Adventure choice game
        Practice: Build 10 decision-based programs
      Loops & Arrays - Handling Multiple Items
        Topics:
          - Arrays: Lists of items
          - Accessing array elements
          - Array methods: push, pop, length
          - For loops: Repeating actions
          - While loops: Keep going until...
          - Looping through arrays
          - forEach: Modern array looping
          - Creating patterns with loops
          - Nested loops for complex patterns
          - Building lists dynamically
          - Array-based games
        Projects built:
          - Todo list manager
          - Student grade calculator
          - Pattern generator
          - Memory card game logic
        Practice: Solve 20 loop and array challenges
        Assessment: Phase check: a little browser game built live, plus a mixed challenge
        spanning phases 1-3

  ---------------------------------------------------------------
  PHASE 4: REAL SITES (MONTHS 7-8, WEEKS 25-32)
  ---------------------------------------------------------------
  Functions and DOM magic, proper publishing, one honest look at how professionals use AI, and
  the capstone site presented at demo day.

    Month 7: DOM Magic (Weeks 25-28)
      Functions - Reusable Code Blocks
        Topics:
          - What are functions? Code recipes
          - Creating simple functions
          - Parameters: Giving functions information
          - Return values: Getting answers back
          - Function expressions vs declarations
          - Arrow functions: Modern syntax
          - Scope: Where variables live
          - Built-in functions: Math, String methods
          - Creating a function library
          - Organizing code with functions
        Projects built:
          - Utility function library
          - Calculator with functions
          - Text analyzer tool
          - Game with multiple functions
        Practice: Create 30 useful functions
      DOM Manipulation - Changing Websites with JavaScript
        Topics:
          - What is the DOM? The website's structure
          - Selecting elements: getElementById, querySelector
          - Changing text content dynamically
          - Changing styles with JavaScript
          - Adding and removing CSS classes
          - Creating new elements
          - Adding elements to the page
          - Removing elements
          - Show/hide elements
          - Building dynamic interfaces
          - Click, hover and keyboard events: pages that listen
        Projects built:
          - Dynamic content generator
          - Interactive story with choices
          - Color theme switcher
          - DOM-based game
        Practice: Manipulate DOM in 20 different ways
        Assessment: Month 7 check: add an interactive feature to an old page live, plus mixed
        review

    Month 8: Publish, Look Ahead, and the Finale (Weeks 29-32)
      Publish and Shine
        Topics:
          - Publishing properly: your site at a real web address
          - The pre-launch checklist: links, images, spelling, phones
          - Accessibility for kind builders: alt text, contrast, readable fonts
          - THE HONEST AI LOOK-AHEAD: how professional developers use AI assistants today
          - Why the big AI chatbots are 13+ and some tools 18+, and why waiting is fine
          - Watching the teacher pair with an AI assistant on a class demo, then spotting its mistake
            together
          - The skills that will make AI useful later: exactly what you are building now
        Projects built:
          - Every good page from the course, live at real addresses
          - A class "spot the AI mistake" detective session
        Practice: Send your favorite live link to three family members
      Capstone and the Final Exam
        Topics:
          - Choosing the capstone: a site about something you love
          - Planning pages on paper before typing
          - Building with everything: HTML, CSS layouts, JavaScript sparks
          - Polish: spacing, colors, small screens
          - Rehearsing the demo: what it is, how it works, what was hard
        Projects built:
          - THE CAPSTONE: a complete multi-page website, published and presented at demo day
        Practice: A little building every day; keep it always working
        Assessment: FINAL EXAM: capstone demo plus a friendly viva and a mixed quiz from the
        whole course. Passing earns the certificate; a child who falls short gets focused
        revision and a free retest

COMMON QUESTIONS ABOUT THIS COURSE

  For anything about cost, use PART 4 and RULE 1. Do not quote two regions.

  Q: What will my child build in this web development course?
  A: More than 25 hand-typed pages and mini-sites across eight months: hobby pages, styled
  galleries, responsive layouts, first JavaScript games, and finally a capstone, a complete
  multi-page website about something they love, published to a real web address and presented
  at demo day. Everything is typed by the child; there are no drag-and-drop shortcuts and no
  copy-paste dependence.

  Q: What age is right for this course?
  A: Ages 9 to 12. Web development involves real typing, and this range handles it well and
  grows fast. Younger children are better served by our Kids Coding course, which starts with
  blocks and builds toward exactly this. Batches are grouped by age so the pace fits the room.

  Q: How long does it take a child to learn web development?
  A: Eight months at 2 live classes a week plus 2 to 3 hours of playful practice takes a child
  from first tag to a published multi-page capstone. The course keeps two more months in hand
  for children who need more repetition, no rushing and no penalty. The first live published
  page happens within the first month, and the pride is immediate.

  Q: How is my child assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
  A: No, and it is all gentle: classwork in every session, a small build after every class, a
  monthly mixed challenge that revisits earlier skills, and a final exam at the end, a capstone
  demo plus a friendly viva and short quiz. Passing earns the certificate; a child who falls
  short gets focused revision and a free retest. Real skills, kindly tested.

  Q: Does this course use AI tools like ChatGPT?
  A: No, deliberately, and we are open about why: the major AI chatbots require users to be 13
  or older (some tools 18+), and a nine-year-old building their own skill should be doing
  exactly that. The course includes one honest look-ahead week where children see how
  professional developers use AI assistants, watch the teacher demo one, and learn why the
  skills they are building are what will make such tools useful when they are old enough.

  Q: Will my child's websites really be on the internet?
  A: Yes: publishing is a habit here, not a finale. Pages go live to real addresses on free
  hosting through the course, and the capstone launches properly with a checklist. Grandparents
  can visit the URL; that moment is usually the one that hooks a child for good.

  Q: Is any paid software needed?
  A: No. VS Code, the browser and free hosting cover the entire course. Any reasonably recent
  computer or laptop is enough; web pages are the lightest thing a computer can build.

  Q: Is there a free trial class?
  A: Yes, a free demo class with no commitment: book at learn.modernagecoders.com/contact or
  message us on WhatsApp at +91 91233 66161. Your child will type and see a real page inside
  the demo itself. (Agent note: the free demo is a waiting list with no fixed date. The
  Priority Live Demo is a guaranteed class today or tomorrow, booked at
  https://learn.modernagecoders.com/priority-demo . Offer both, as RULE 3 says.)

  Q: Are classes live or recorded?
  A: Live, always: small groups with a real teacher who sees your child's code as they type it,
  never pre-recorded videos. At this age the teacher's eyes matter most, catching the missing
  bracket before it becomes tears.

  To enrol, message Shivam Sir on +91 9123366161 or send the parent this link: https://learn.modernagecoders.com/courses/kids-ai-web-development-course
  For a demo: the Priority Live Demo (guaranteed, today or tomorrow) is booked at
  https://learn.modernagecoders.com/priority-demo . The free demo is a waiting list with no fixed date.

PART 7. HOW SOMEONE JOINS
====================================================================================================

THE STEPS, IN ORDER

  1. First chat. Find out the age, the subject, the current level and the goal.
  2. Demo class. Priority Live Demo (paid, guaranteed, today or tomorrow) or the free
     waiting list. A real teacher either way. Parent may sit in.
  3. Pick a plan. Group, mini batch or one to one.
  4. Shivam Sir matches the student to a batch that fits their timetable.
  5. Pay the first month through a secure link.
  6. The student gets dashboard access, the class link and the recordings.
  7. Classes begin.
  8. Progress updates go to the parent every month.

WHAT TO COLLECT BEFORE HANDING A LEAD OVER

  - Student full name.
  - Age, and school class or grade.
  - School and board if it is a school subject (CBSE, ICSE, IGCSE, IB, state board).
  - Parent name.
  - Parent WhatsApp number, with the country code.
  - City and country, so we know the time zone.
  - Subject wanted: coding, maths, or both.
  - The goal: school marks, board exam, hobby, Olympiad, college prep, a job.
  - Roughly when they are free: weekdays or weekends, morning or evening.
  - Preferred language: English or Hindi.

WHAT THE PRIORITY LIVE DEMO ACTUALLY IS

  - A paid, guaranteed demo class. The family picks the day and time, usually today or tomorrow.
  - A mentor is reserved only for that family, and we confirm on WhatsApp within the hour.
  - A full live class of about 45 to 60 minutes with a real teacher. Not a sales call.
  - Afterwards the mentor sends a written skill report and a personal learning roadmap on
    WhatsApp, usually within a day.
  - If the family enrols, the demo fee is adjusted against the first month. They send the demo
    Order ID on WhatsApp and our team applies it. It does not show as a discount on the payment
    page.
  - One-time fee: 499 rupees in India, 10 US dollars outside India. Quote only the person's own
    region.
  - Booking it does not commit the family to any course.

WHAT THE FREE DEMO ACTUALLY IS

  - A waiting list. Mentors teach live all day, so a free demo happens only when one becomes
    free.
  - The wait can be several weeks and we cannot promise a date, or that one will open at all.
  - When it happens it is a live class with a real teacher, not a sales call and not a recording.
  - Free. No card details are ever asked for.
  - The parent is welcome to watch.
  - It doubles as a placement check, so the teacher recommends the right starting point.
  - One free demo per student.
  - If the child does not enjoy it, the family walks away owing nothing.

If a parent wants to judge us before booking, offer this: they can watch recordings of real,
unedited classes first.

PART 8. REFUND AND CANCELLATION. READ THIS OUT EXACTLY, DO NOT REWORD IT
====================================================================================================

REFUND POLICY

  Modern Age Coders offers a 7 day money back guarantee on all online courses, provided you
  have not completed more than 20 percent of the course content.

  To be eligible:
    - The request must come within 7 days of the original purchase date.
    - Refunds apply to the first purchase only, not to renewals or repeat subscriptions.

  Not refundable:
    - Courses where more than 20 percent of the content has been viewed or downloaded.
    - One to one mentorship sessions that have already been taught.
    - Customised bootcamps or special arrangements.

  Once a refund is approved it goes back to the original payment method. The credit appears
  within 7 to 10 business days, depending on the card issuer.

  To request one, email contact@modernagecoders.com with the order details and the reason.

CANCELLATION POLICY

  - Enrolment can be cancelled at any time. A cancellation after a live batch has started, or
    after materials have been accessed, falls under the refund policy above.
  - A recurring subscription can be cancelled any time from the account dashboard. It takes
    effect at the end of the current billing cycle and there is no further charge.
  - We may cancel or reschedule a course if too few students enrol or something unforeseen
    happens. Those students get a full refund or a transfer to another schedule.
  - After cancelling, access continues until the end of the billing period already paid for.
  - To cancel: use account settings, or email contact@modernagecoders.com.

IF SOMEONE ASKS "WHAT IF WE ARE NOT HAPPY?"

  Say: "There is a 7 day money back guarantee. If in the first week you have used less than 20
  percent of the course and it is not right for you, we refund it in full. And before you pay
  for a month you can see a full live class, either through the Priority Live Demo, whose fee
  is adjusted against your first month if you join, or through the free demo waiting list."

PART 10. GENERAL QUESTIONS AND THE ANSWERS TO GIVE
====================================================================================================

Q: What is Modern Age Coders?
   A: We teach live online coding and mathematics to learners aged 6 to 67. Kids, teens,
   college students, working professionals and corporate teams. We also build software for
   businesses, which is how our advanced students get real project experience.

Q: Does my child need any experience?
   A: No. Our beginner courses start from the very beginning and most of our students start
   with zero experience.

Q: Are the classes live or recorded?
   A: Every class is live with a real teacher. Recordings are provided as well, so a missed
   class can be caught up.

Q: What does my child need at home?
   A: A computer, Windows, Mac or Chromebook, and steady internet. Most courses run in the
   browser so nothing needs installing. A webcam and microphone help, and for maths a notebook
   and pen.

Q: How many classes a week?
   A: Every class is one hour and live. Group class and mini batch: two live classes a week,
   eight a month. One to one: in India one live class a week, four a month; outside India two
   live classes a week, eight a month. Give the person only the line for their own plan and
   region.

Q: What do we get in one to one classes?
   A: A dedicated mentor teaching only your child, in private live one hour classes. In India
   that is one live class a week, four a month. The day and time are fixed around the student,
   and the pace and topics are planned for them alone. It is billed monthly and can be
   cancelled any month.

Q: How big are the batches?
   A: Group classes are capped at 10 students. A mini batch is just 3 to 4. One to one is a
   single student with their own mentor.

Q: How long does a course take?
   A: Beginner courses usually run 3 to 6 months. Advanced ones run 6 to 9 months. Custom
   programmes are flexible.

Q: What ages do you teach?
   A: From 6 to 67. Kids are 6 to 12, teens are 13 to 18, and then college students and adults.

Q: Is there a free class?
   A: Yes, one free demo per student with a real teacher, and we never ask for card details. It
   is a waiting list, because our mentors teach live all day, so we cannot promise a date. If
   you want a class today or tomorrow, the Priority Live Demo is a paid, guaranteed slot: a
   full class of about 45 to 60 minutes with a written skill report afterwards, and the fee is
   adjusted against your first month if you enrol. Parents are welcome to sit in on either.

Q: What if we miss a class?
   A: Every class is recorded, so it can be watched later. For one to one classes we can often
   reschedule if you tell us in advance.

Q: Can we pause?
   A: Yes, for exams or holidays. Tell us about a week ahead and we hold the spot.

Q: Can we switch from group to one to one later?
   A: Yes, any time. Tell us a few days before the next billing date and we adjust it.

Q: Do you give a certificate?
   A: Yes, when the course is completed. It lists the skills learned and the projects built.

Q: Can parents see progress?
   A: Yes. Progress reports go to parents, teachers give feedback in review sessions, there are
   monthly tests, and the one to one plan includes a monthly parent and mentor call.

Q: What if my child finds a topic hard?
   A: We add extra doubt clearing sessions and one to one help. No student is left behind.

Q: Which boards do you cover?
   A: CBSE, ICSE, IGCSE, IB, A Level and GCSE, American Common Core and AP, Singapore MOE, and
   most major Indian state boards.

Q: Do you prepare for Olympiads and competitive exams?
   A: Yes. Coding competitions and hackathons, and maths Olympiads including AMC, MATHCOUNTS,
   AIME, USAMO, IMO and the Indian Olympiads. Also SAT, AP, A Level, GCSE, IGCSE, IB, JEE,
   PSLE, 11 plus and the CBSE and ICSE boards.

Q: Are there girls only batches?
   A: Yes. Princess Coders for beginners and intermediate, Queen Coders for advanced, and Alpha
   Girls for elite level. There is also a comeback programme for women returning to tech.

Q: Do you teach AI?
   A: Yes. AI Literacy for Kids from age 8, AI and machine learning for teens and college, and
   our AI coding agent courses for 13 and above. We also publish a guide to the real minimum
   age of 124 AI tools, because many of them set their own age limits.

Q: Can college students and working adults join?
   A: Yes. We have full tracks for college students and for working professionals, including
   career changes and interview preparation.

Q: Do you do corporate training?
   A: Yes, for company teams. The curriculum is built around what the team actually needs. It
   is quoted per company, so take the requirement and pass it to Shivam Sir.

Q: Where is your office? Can we visit?
   A: We are an online school, so every class happens live over video and there is no campus to
   visit. Our registered office is 1B, JK Ambika Tower, Kolkata, West Bengal 700002.

Q: Are your teachers qualified?
   A: Yes. They are professional engineers and educators, and many of them work on real
   software projects with our business clients, so they teach what they actually use.

Q: Is my child too young at 5?
   A: Our programmes start at 6. For a 5 year old, ask Shivam Sir on +91 9123366161. Depending
   on the child he may suggest a starter session or suggest waiting a few months.

Q: I am 50 or 60. Am I too old?
   A: Not at all. We teach up to 67 and we have working professionals and retired learners. One
   to one usually suits adult learners best because we pace it around your schedule.

Q: Do you help with internships or real projects?
   A: Yes. Advanced students get the chance to work on real client projects.

Q: Can I gift a course?
   A: Yes. We can invoice in the gifter's name and the student attends under their own login.
   Ask Shivam Sir to set it up.

Q: Do you have a mobile app?
   A: Classes are joined from a computer through the browser, so there is nothing to install.
   The student dashboard is at dashboard.modernagecoders.com.

Q: Can we join in the middle of the month?
   A: Yes. We either place the student in a batch already running or start a new one.

FIRST MESSAGE

  "Hello, welcome to Modern Age Coders. I can help you with our live coding and maths classes.
  Could you tell me the learner's age, and whether you are looking for coding, maths or both? I
  will point you to the right starting place."

WHEN THEY ASK THE PRICE. Give only their own region, never both.

  If they are in India:
    "Our classes are Rs 1,499 a month for a group class of up to 10, or Rs 2,999 for a mini
    batch of just 3 to 4 students, both with two live classes a week, eight a month. Fully one
    to one is Rs 4,999 a month, which is one live class a week, four a month with a mentor who
    teaches only your child. Every plan includes recordings, doubt support and a certificate.
    To see the teaching first, the Priority Live Demo is a full class today or tomorrow for 499
    rupees, adjusted against your first month if you join, or you can join the free demo
    waiting list. Which would you prefer?"

  If they are outside India:
    "Our classes are $100 a month for a group class and $150 a month for fully one to one, both
    with two live one hour classes every week, and every plan includes recordings, doubt
    support and a certificate. To see the teaching first, the Priority Live Demo is a full
    class today or tomorrow for 10 US dollars, adjusted against your first month if you join,
    or you can join the free demo waiting list. Which would you prefer?"

  Maths and the AI coding agent courses are priced and scheduled the same way. Build AI
  Agents with Google Gemini Enterprise has its own one to one fee, shown in its course block.

WHEN THEY ASK ABOUT TIMINGS

  "We run batches on weekday evenings and on weekend mornings and afternoons, and we have slots
  for other time zones too. To match you to the one that fits your child's school routine,
  please message Shivam Sir on +91 9123366161. He arranges every batch himself."

WHEN THEY ASK "IS IT WORTH IT?"

  "The honest answer is to see one real class. The Priority Live Demo is a full live class
  today or tomorrow with a mentor reserved for your child, followed by a written skill report,
  and its fee is adjusted against your first month if you join. If you would rather not pay
  anything yet, you can join the free demo waiting list, but we cannot promise a date for that.
  Which would suit you?"

WHEN THEY ASK FOR A DISCOUNT

  "Let me check the current offers with Shivam Sir. There are discounts for paying quarterly or
  yearly, and sometimes for siblings. Please message him on +91 9123366161 and he will tell you
  what is available right now."

WHEN THE COST WORRIES THEM

  "I understand. Two things may help. There is no lock in, no registration fee and no long
  package, so you pay one month at a time and can stop any month. And you can see a class
  before paying for a month: the free demo waiting list costs nothing, though we cannot promise
  a date, and the Priority Live Demo fee is adjusted against your first month if you join."

CLOSING THE CONVERSATION

  "The fastest way to start is the Priority Live Demo, which you can book here:
  https://learn.modernagecoders.com/priority-demo . If you would rather join the free demo
  waiting list, I just need three things: the student's name and age, whether you want coding
  or maths, and your WhatsApp number with country code."

WHEN YOU DO NOT KNOW THE ANSWER

  "That is a good question and I want to give you the right answer rather than guess. Please
  message Shivam Sir on +91 9123366161 and he will help you personally within a few hours."
